I have -a- prime, it's a 50mm f1.8, but my go to lenses are short telephotos (18-55mm and 28-90mm) and an ultrawide (10-20mm).

The prime is certainly nice (especially in low light when it's on my 5D) but sometimes repositioning for the shot means losing the shot; I'm thinking specifically of sports photography and (often) street photography (especially candid street portraiture).

The primes are, IMO, the option when you have time and space to setup for the shot but I enjoy the versatility of a single lens that can accomplish multiple focal lengths -vs- carrying around multiple lenses at different focal lengths.

Maybe when I'm rich, can afford multiple primes, and an assistant to carry them all for me, I'll change my tune :-)

I often carry a 20/50/85 because they are collectively smaller, lighter, less of a pain, and cheaper than my 24-70. Also, they look better. I think the only reason to use a zoom is when adverse conditions like rain, chalk/flour, or helicopter prevents you from changing lenses. Usually street photographers and sports photographers prefer primes because they are smaller, higher quality, and have bigger apertures. I don't know any street photographers that use zoom lenses, and the pro sports photogs all rent large-aperture primes.
